figures.caption: Figure 1: DRAFT recovers where walls and floor are on a held-out route. (a) Four views of scene 4: frame (not an input), furnished (F) and empty-room (E) ground truth, DRAFT (D), BrainDiffuser (BD) detail with the DRAFT layout (B), and layout r of D and B against F and E. (b) Merged surface of D from above, blue within 25 cm of F. Hand-picked route, ranked 60th in layout r and 94th in F-score of 324 routes. Rule-chosen routes: Figure 7 and Section K.

Figure 2: Overview of DRAFT: the coarse layout is fixed before the detail. (a) The readout maps EVC and camera motion to the layout code, which (b) a renderer and generator turn into eight depth maps. (c) Trajectory and fusion heads give the DRAFT layout, which (d) sets the broad structure of any depth map before range calibration and lifting to 3D. Real data of the Figure 1 route, except the noise z0.

Table 1: Main results: fusion gives the best layout at no measurable cost in surface accuracy. Each layout replaces the broad structure of one generator’s depth. C: EVC, M: camera motion (12 readout regressors, 72 trajectory-head features), T: free space. Row: row order, L/R: left/right, bold: best, underline: second. Layout, MAE: 324-route means, others: ten-scene means. Last rows: DRAFT minus generator alone (∗: 95% paired scene-bootstrap CI excludes zero).

Table 2: Comparison with fMRI decoders: every decoder scores best with the DRAFT layout, and none matches it given only the camera path. Alone: unmodified. + path, + DRAFT: with the trajectory layout (camera path only) or the DRAFT layout, post hoc except for linear depth and Brain-Diffuser. Averaging as in Table 1. Bold: row best. ∗: 95% CI of the gain over alone excludes zero (Table 5). Unmodified MindEye and Brain-Diffuser keep slightly higher F-scores than DRAFT. Decoders: 418 recordings, DRAFT: 416. ‡DA V2 on the frames. †Our adaptation (Section C.1).

Table 3: Layout r gains of DRAFT hold in nine or ten scenes, and surface gains are smaller. Ten-scene means of paired differences (positive: first better), 95% paired scene-bootstrap CI, scenes favoring the first. r: layout r, BD: Brain-Diffuser, M, T: as in Table 1, cosine: similarity of centered codes. MAE, Chamfer in m. Sign-flip p: a0.002, b0.004, c0.012, d0.025, others untested.

Figure 3: EVC predicts the layout code best of the tested regions. (a) Template masks, not individual localizers. (b) Held-out r per layout-code entry (ten-scene mean), from motion alone or with 1,000 voxels of one mask. (c) Per-scene differences in cosine similarity to the true code.

Figure 4: Surface scores separate methods less than layout scores do. (a to d) Display route (scene 6), one of the top five for DRAFT among routes where DRAFT and BD + DRAFT layout beat unmodified Brain-Diffuser (BD) in F-score. b to d: true points below 2.4 m by distance to the nearest prediction (F: F-score, R: recall, Figure 6). On rule-chosen routes, DRAFT has the lowest F-score of the generator, DRAFT and BD + DRAFT layout in seven of ten (Table 9). (e) Layout r gain over the fixed template. (f) Post hoc F-score gain over a wrong scene.

Table 5: Given the same camera path, DRAFT has a higher layout r than every decoder, and the DRAFT layout improves every decoder. (a) DRAFT minus each method of Table 2. (b) The markers of Table 2: decoder with the DRAFT layout and range calibration (a = 2) minus unmodified decoder (a = 1), ∗ if the interval excludes zero. The surface gains of Brain-Diffuser and MindEye are not reliable. Ten-scene means of per-scene differences, 95% paired scene-bootstrap intervals and scenes of ten favoring DRAFT or the layout. Post hoc exact sign-flip p (Section B) for (b) and the trajectory-layout rows of (a). Layout rows are post hoc except for linear depth and Brain-Diffuser (Section C.2). ‡DA V2 on the frames. †Our adaptation (Section C.1).

Figure 5: EVC’s gain over camera motion peaks at a 3 to 4 s lag and exceeds all 20 circular shifts. Gain: cosine similarity of the EVC readout minus that of motion alone. (a) Single-second BOLD lags. Dots: scenes (hollow and numbered at or below zero). Diamonds and bars: mean and 95% paired scene-bootstrap interval. Shading and dashed line: the 2 to 5 s window of the main readout, which averages four lags and can gain more than any single one. (b) Circular shifts of 10 to 70 s (gray) and the unshifted window (teal), on the scale of (a).

Table 7: Replacing or shifting the brain input worsens layout and surfaces in most scenes. Intact minus control, for feature replacement (readout kept) and circular shift (readout refitted). Ten-scene means with 95% paired scene-bootstrap intervals (low, high). Scenes better: of ten, scenes in which the intact input scores better (per-scene values omitted; Section K). Pixel MAE and Chamfer in cm (m in the other tables), F in percentage points (pp). G: generator, D: DRAFT, subscript: a. Only one mean favors the control, G2 Chamfer under feature replacement, within noise.

Figure 6: Three routes chosen for display, not representative: predictions recover the room’s extent and main wall positions, not clear walls or furniture. Rule: among routes where DRAFT and Brain-Diffuser + DRAFT layout beat unmodified Brain-Diffuser (Brain-Diffuser alone) in Fscore, highest DRAFT F-score first, one per scene, without the route of Figure 4 (rule-chosen routes: Table 9). Brain-Diffuser alone: Table 2. Row 1 (found): true points by distance to the nearest prediction (R: recall). Row 2 (predicted): predicted points by distance to the ground truth (P: precision). Points above 2.4 m or outside the plotted area, and in row 2 stray points (fewer than 4 neighbors or clusters under 40 points, radii scaled with range), are hidden for display, but all points are scored. F: route F-score (bold: best of three).

Figure 7: Depth atlas, scenes 1 to 4, failures included: on the ten rule-chosen routes, BrainDiffuser + DRAFT layout has the highest route layout r in six scenes, DRAFT in three and unmodified Brain-Diffuser in one. All eight views, 1 s apart, of the rule-chosen routes of Table 9 (Figure 1 is hand-picked). Rows: furnished ground truth (GT, gray: invalid), DRAFT (D, a = 2), unmodified Brain-Diffuser (U, calibrated DA V2 depth, a = 1) and Brain-Diffuser + DRAFT layout (B, a = 2). Numbers: route layout r (bold: best of three) and the scene’s value over all routes (in parentheses). Means over these ten and all 324 routes: 0.493 and 0.480 (D), 0.236 and 0.324 (U), 0.509 and 0.493 (B). Scenes 5 to 10: Section K.

Table 9: On the ten atlas routes DRAFT improves the layout, but its F-score is the lowest of the three methods in seven routes. Scores of the ten atlas routes, whose surface atlas is listed in Section K, all at a = 2. G: generator, D: DRAFT, BD + L: Brain-Diffuser + DRAFT layout (surfaces only). Bold per row: best of three for surfaces. Mean: over the ten routes. Bottom: paired differences with 95% route-bootstrap intervals and routes where D is better.

Table 10: Once per-view depth scale is removed by alignment, the methods with a DRAFT or trajectory layout score best. (a) Means over ten held-out scenes at a = 1. Alignment uses test depth (post hoc). F: F-score at 25 cm. SI-log: ×100. Bold, underline: best and second best per column, ties share a mark. (b) Paired differences, 95% paired scene-bootstrap intervals, scenes favoring the first method and sign-flip p (Section B). †First minus second. BD: Brain-Diffuser.

Table 11: The DRAFT layout lowers the change in 3D error between views for every source at both factors, but at a = 1 it lowers the F-score of DRAFT and Brain-Diffuser. Eight-view F-score and one-second change in 3D error E1 of Equation (11) over the 72 views of each video. Ten-scene means with 95% scene-bootstrap intervals (paired for differences). Bold, underline: best and second best. Bottom: with minus without the DRAFT layout. BD: Brain-Diffuser.

Table 12: Wrong-scene predictions keep most of the F-score. Upper rows: the fixed template scored as a prediction. Lower rows: predictions for the next held-out scene lifted at the evaluated poses (post hoc), and the gain of the correct scene, with its 95% paired scene-bootstrap interval and the number of scenes (of ten) with a positive gain. Ten-scene means. –: not applicable, since the template is the same for every scene. Brain-Diffuser and MindEye at their best factor, a = 1.

Table 13: Without range calibration (a = 1), fusion lowers the F-score and raises the Chamfer distance. Calibration raises the F-score of every layout except the generator’s and lowers it for the image decoders. C: EVC, M: camera motion, T: free-space features. Layout r and pixel MAE: 324-route means, F-score and Chamfer distance: ten-scene means, as in Table 1. Bold, underline: best and second best current method. Small lines: a = 2 minus a = 1, 95% paired scene-bootstrap interval. DRAFT minus generator: ten-scene means of per-scene differences (∗: interval excludes zero). †Fixed after earlier results on these scenes. BD: Brain-Diffuser.

Table 14: At each method’s best factor, DRAFT surfaces are no better than those of the generator or the image decoders. (a) F-score and Chamfer distance for a from 1 to 3 (bold: best a, chosen on the held-out scenes, paired differences in Table 15). (b) Precision and recall at a = 2 and at the best a, and DRAFT minus the row (–: reference, bold: best at a = 2, the a = 1 block is summarized in Section K). Ten-scene means, 95% paired scene-bootstrap intervals.

Table 15: Choosing a without the scored scene leaves DRAFT within noise of, or worse than, the generator and the image decoders. For each held-out scene, a ∈ {1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3} is chosen by the Chamfer distance or F-score of the other nine. (a) Chosen a, folds choosing it, and scores (bold: best over both selections). (b) DRAFT minus each method, 95% paired scene-bootstrap interval, scenes of ten favoring DRAFT. Ten-scene means.

Table 16: Post hoc primary tests: two support a hypothesis, three are null and one goes against it. Estimate: ten-scene mean and 95% paired scene-bootstrap interval. Scenes: scenes of ten with a positive value. p: exact sign-flip. Holm: adjusted over the six tests. Outcome: the decision rule written before the analysis. ∗A time-misaligned brain component gives the same slope, so this test does not show brain signal (text). †The hypothesis predicted a negative value.

Table 17: Five withheld scenes: DRAFT beats the fixed template in every scene, but the brain’s contribution replicates within only two. Layout r, route-pooled. Differences: DRAFT minus the named layout, with 95% participant cluster bootstrap intervals that omit variation between routes. ∗Replicated (positive, Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 over the three contrasts of the scene). Mean: mean of the five differences, positive scenes and exact one-sided sign-flip p (1/32 is the smallest attainable value, and the scenes are not independent, see text). Development: ten-scene mean and range of the differences (layout r of DRAFT 0.359 to 0.578).
